name: Off-Highway Motorcycle
description: A motorized off-highway vehicle on two wheels with a seat the rider straddles and handlebars, the category a dirt e-moto is ridden under off the road; it's registered with the Department of Natural Resources rather than for the highway. Defined by Minnesota Statutes §84.787, subd. 7, which excludes electric-assisted bicycles.

restrictions.rule: Two wheels, a seat or saddle the rider straddles, and handlebars
No limit on motor power or speed; an electric-assisted bicycle isn't one
Registered with the DNR for three years, with a decal on its side; the decal needn't be displayed on private property
A nonresident may ride state and grant-in-aid trails on a nonresident off-highway motorcycle trail pass instead of registering
No one under 18 may register one
Riders under 16 need a DNR off-highway motorcycle safety certificate to ride on public lands or waters
Riders under 12 need someone 18 or older with them to ride on public lands
Riders under 18 must wear a helmet; every rider must wear eye protection
Ridden on DNR trails designated for off-highway motorcycles or multiple use, on approved corridor access trails, or on private land
Kept off town road and county and state-aid highway rights-of-way except on designated trails, and never within an interstate or freeway right-of-way
